theory.intro: The **surface area** of a prism is the total area of all its faces, which is the area of its net. Find the area of every face and add them. A prism has two identical end faces plus one rectangle per side of them.
facts: For a right-angled or isosceles triangular face, a slant edge is often not given — find it with Pythagoras' theorem before working out the rectangles.
An **open** container (no lid) leaves one face off, so add only the faces that are actually there.
Keep every length in the same unit; surface area is in square units ($\text{cm}^{2}$, $\text{m}^{2}$).
steps: Identify every face of the prism.
If a slant edge is unknown, find it using Pythagoras' theorem.
Find the area of each face.
Add the areas of all the faces.

foundation.solution_text:
$A_1 = (8\times 4)\times 2$
$= 64\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = (5\times 4)\times 2$
$= 40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (8\times 5)\times 2$
$= 80\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 184\text{ cm}^{2}$

A cube has $6$ identical square faces.
$\text{SA} = 6\times 5^{2}$
$= 6\times 25$
$= 150\text{ cm}^{2}$

$A_1 = 2\times\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 4$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = 6\times 12$
$= 72\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (5\times 12)\times 2$
$= 120\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 216\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.solution_text:
The height meets the base at its midpoint, so half the base is $4$ cm.
$x^{2} = 4^{2} + 3^{2}$
$= 25$
$x = 5\text{ cm}$
$A_1 = 2\times\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 3$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = 8\times 10$
$= 80\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (5\times 10)\times 2$
$= 100\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 204\text{ cm}^{2}$

The box has no top face, so add the base and the four side faces.
$A_1 = 6\times 4$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = (6\times 5)\times 2$
$= 60\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (4\times 5)\times 2$
$= 40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 124\text{ cm}^{2}$

Here $x$ is a shorter side, so subtract inside Pythagoras' theorem.
$x^{2} = 10^{2} - 6^{2}$
$= 64$
$x = 8\text{ cm}$
$A_1 = 2\times\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 6$
$= 48\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = 8\times 9$
$= 72\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = 6\times 9$
$= 54\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_4 = 10\times 9$
$= 90\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3 + A_4$
$= 264\text{ cm}^{2}$

mastery.solution_text:
$A_{\text{tri}} = 2\times\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 4$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
The three rectangles have widths $5$, $5$ and $6$, and length $x$.
$A_{\text{rect}} = (5+5+6)x$
$= 16x$
$\text{SA} = A_{\text{tri}} + A_{\text{rect}}$
$184 = 24 + 16x$
$16x = 160$
$x = 10\text{ cm}$

$\text{SA} = 2(2\times 1.5 + 2\times 1 + 1.5\times 1)$
$= 2(3 + 2 + 1.5)$
$= 13\text{ m}^{2}$
$13\div 4 = 3.25$
Tins cannot be split, so $4$ tins are needed.
$4\times 8 = 32$
